title: Counterexamples to the Balogh-Linz-Patkós Conjecture
summary: A set system $\mathcal{F}$ is called $t$-intersecting if $|A\cap B|\ge t$ for every pair of sets $A,B\in \mathcal{F}.$ A set system $\mathcal{F}$ is $k$-Sperner if it does not contain a chain of length $k+1$. Balogh, Linz and Patkós (Combinatorial Theory, 2023) conjectured an extremal result for $t$-intersecting $k$-Sperner families when $n+t$ is odd. In this note we give an explicit construction that is $t$-intersecting and $k$-Sperner, and whose size exceeds that of the conjectured fixed-star construction for infinitely many values of $n$.
